description:
Gating scoping bead. Everything downstream depends on the answer, so do this before writing any flowsheet code.

THE PROBLEM: HTR-10 is 10 MWth. A modest crude distillation unit furnace is tens to a hundred MW. The reactor cannot run a whole refinery, so the honest deliverable is a bounded process-heat demonstration, not a plant.

WHAT TO ESTABLISH:
1. Heat demand curve of each candidate refinery duty (crude preheat, atmospheric furnace, reboilers, reformer) in MW and at what temperature.
2. Available helium outlet temperature and duty from the HTR-10 model, and what fraction of each duty it can actually supply.
3. Temperature match: HTR-10 helium outlet is high enough for crude heating by a wide margin, but steam reforming sits near the top of the range. State which duties are reachable and which are not.
4. Choose the demonstration scope explicitly. Options include a single reachable duty at true 10 MWth scale, a scaled multi-module plant, or a deliberately labelled scale-up. Whichever is chosen, the scale assumption must be stated in the simulator UI and docs, not buried.

ACCEPTANCE: a written energy and temperature balance with numbers, and one recorded decision on scope. No fabricated figures — derive from the model and cited open literature.
title: refinery: DECISION — energy balance and temperature match, then pick the demonstration scope

title: provenance: add missing LICENSE/NOTICE to thermochimica, onix, moltres

description:
Batched **root finding** across the three backends.

Existing serial code to build on, not replace:

- `src/polynomial/` — `linear_eqn.rs`, `quadratic_eqn.rs`, `cubic_eqn.rs`,
  `roots.rs` (closed-form/analytic roots).
- `src/math/` — `erf_inv.rs`, `inv_inc_gamma.rs` (iterative inversions).
- The JANAF thermo Newton solve and the `PengRobinsonGas` Z-root selection are
  the real per-cell callers (see `op-sisf`, `op-17ke`).

What to add:

- A **batched** entry point: solve N independent scalar root problems at once
  (one per cell/face), which is the shape that actually maps onto a GPU. A
  single root solve should stay serial — say so in the docs.
- Bracketing + safeguarded methods, not bare Newton: bisection, Brent /
  safeguarded Newton-with-fallback. Divergent or non-bracketed cases must
  return an error per lane, not poison the whole batch.
- **Per-lane convergence flags** returned to the caller — on a GPU every lane
  runs the same iteration count, so a lane that failed must be identifiable
  rather than silently returning its last iterate.
- Closed-form polynomial roots (quadratic/cubic) get their own batched kernel;
  they are branch-light and a good first GPU target.

V&V: analytic roots for the polynomial cases; CPU serial as oracle for the
iterative ones; record measured max/RMS error and the tolerance in the doc
comment.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
Implementation landed on branch claude/outram-foam-8ookor (uncommitted working tree; maintainer to review/commit).

New files:
- crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/src/math/parallel.rs
- crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/src/math/parallel/tests.rs
Edited: crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/src/math/mod.rs (pub mod parallel + pub use only).

Module home is math/, not polynomial/: the general solver takes a caller-supplied residual (h(T) - h_target) which is not a polynomial, and math/ already hosts the crate's iterative inversions.

Public API (one entry point per operation, ComputeBackend a parameter):
solve_bracketed_batch (RootMethod::{Bisection, Brent}), solve_newton_batch
(bracket-safeguarded Newton, value+derivative closure), linear/quadratic/
cubic_roots_batch (wrappers over the existing scalar closed-form solvers),
root_batch_backend_for / poly_roots_backend_for, plus RootProblem,
RootSettings, RootMethod, RootStatus, RootSolution, RootBatch,
RootBatchFailure.

Per-lane convergence flags as the epic requires: RootSolution::root() returns
Option<f64>, Some only when Converged; RootBatch::roots() returns
Err(RootBatchFailure) naming failure count and first failing lane. A
non-converged lane is never clamped to a bracket endpoint.

Results are BITWISE identical Serial vs CpuMulti at 1/2/4/8 worker threads
(asserted, not argued) for a pure residual closure - no cross-lane arithmetic
exists, unlike a reduction.

Measured on 4 logical cores, release, --features parallel (2026-08-12):
- ROOT_BATCH_MIN_PROBLEMS = 256 (crate-wide placeholder 4096 is 16x too high
  for this kernel; crossover moves with the caller's residual cost - cheap
  closure 256, costly closure ~128-256).
- POLY_ROOTS_MIN_EQUATIONS = 1024, POLY_BLOCK = 256.
- Thread scaling on 65536 imbalanced lanes: 1.91x @2, 2.73x-3.66x @4, no
  further gain @8 (compute-bound, unlike the memory-bound field kernels).
Fourth measured crossover in the crate; the spread is now 256 / 4096 /
131072 / 262144. Input to op-yvj.4.7.

Gates: lib 425 (default) / 427 (parallel), doc 74 both, all green in release.
cargo check --all-targets --target aarch64-linux-android passes under both
feature settings. No GPU kernel - Gpu requests degrade to the best CPU path.

STILL OUTSTANDING (maintainer): wire src/prelude.rs and the README ported-items
table; those files were deliberately not touched.

title: outram-foam-basic-lib: batched root finding (bracketed/Newton/Brent + closed-form poly roots) on the hybrid backend
